To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cortico-subthalamic nucleus projection is one of multiple innervation sites of long-range corticospinal tract axons, and that corticospinal axons are not exclusively involved in direct motor control.
the STN receives a small number of long-range corticospinal axons from the frontal cortex and that these same axons also innervate multiple brain sites other than the STN.
the subthalamic nucleaus is innervated by a small fraction of long-range corticifugal axons, most of which also emit collatersals that innervates multiple brain sites other than the STN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the anatomical organization of the cortico-STNA projection.
the neural basis of the basal ganglia and its role in movement and cognition.
the role of the subthalamic (STN) nucleus in basal ganglia function, and how the nucleus is connected to the cerebral cortex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cortico-subcortical motor circuit consists of multiple long-range corticostriato-thalamo-STN pathways.
the STN is one of the multiple innervation sites for the long-range corticospinal system.

STN receives efferent motor commands from the motor cortex, but also receives associative motor commands from the associative cortices, which are relayed through the associative thalamic relay nuclei.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the frontal cortical layer V neurons are not the sole source of cortico-STN projections and that corticofugal projections to the STN are part of a multiple innervation system that may play a role in associative control of motor behavior.
STN is one of the multiple innervation sites for a small fraction of long-range corticocortical axons, which originate from small-to-medium-sized layer V pyramidal cells.

the frontal cortex provides a wide variety of long-range corticocortical and corticofugal projections to multiple brain sites, and that the corticofugal innervation of the basal ganglia is one of these multiple projections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cortico-stn projection is formed by collaterals from long-range corticospinal axons that also innervate multiple brain sites.
the STN receives corticofugal input from a wide variety of cortical areas.
the STN is not a simple relay station of efferent copies, but rather a site of integration for cortical inputs that are involved in the associative control of movement.
